page: Amazon Web Services x8g.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the arm64-based AWS Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz, with a single thread per core. The instance is equipped with 1024.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. No GPUs are included.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier memory performance, with cached and uncached memory bandwidth read and write speeds placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores in the top 25% and top 10% respectively. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top 10%, alongside static web serving throughput. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and text processing benchmarks scoring in the middle 50%.

The x8g.16xlarge delivers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads due to its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and Arm-based architecture, which typically offers a lower cost-to-performance ratio compared to traditional x86 architectures. The primary tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware, meaning storage-heavy or GPU-accelerated workloads must rely on network-attached resources.
This instance is suited for memory-intensive applications, large-scale database operations, in-memory caching platforms like Redis, software compilation, and static web serving.
